newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Fourteen N.Koreans seek asylum in South Korea.
newsitem.headline: Fourteen N.Koreans seek asylum in South Korea.

text.p: The South Korean navy on Monday intercepted a boat carrying 14 North Koreans seeking to defect, a defence ministry spokesman said.
He said the boat was spotted off the west coast of the Korean peninsula and was being escorted to an undisclosed South Korean port.
It was one of the biggest defections ever from North Korea since the Korean peninsula was divided at the end of World War Two.
The largest was a group of 17 -- including 16 members of a single family -- that arrived in South Korea last December after a six-week long epic escape down the length of China and into Hong Kong.
"The boat was spotted 5.7 miles (9.2 km) southwest of Paengnyong island," the spokesman said. The island is close to the military demarcation line separating the two Koreas.

Last Friday, a North Korean worker seeking asylum flew into Seoul from an unnamed third country. A growing number of North Koreans have been fleeing hunger and economic ruin in their communist homeland.
